A larger square with side length 3 is placed at the bottom of the triangle, its bottom side on the triangle's base, and the two ends of its top side touching the two slanted sides of the triangle. A smaller square with side length 2 is placed directly above the large square, the two vertices of its bottom side on the top side of the large square, and the two vertices of its top side touching the two slanted sides of the triangle. Reasoning: Let the triangle's base length be B, and its height be H. In the triangle, the length of a horizontal cross-section parallel to the base changes linearly with height, so at height y from the base, the width is B(1 - y/H). The large square has side length 3, so at height y=3, the triangle's width is 3: B(1 - 3/H)=3. The small square has side length 2 and is located above the large square, so its top side is at height y=3+2=5, and the triangle's width is 2: B(1 - 5/H)=2. Subtracting the two equations gives 2B/H=1, so B/H=1/2. Substitute into B(1 - 3/H)=3 to get B - 3B/H = 3, namely B - 3/2 = 3, so B=9/2. Thus H=9. The triangle's area is (1/2)BH = (1/2)(9/2)(9)=81/4=20 1/4.
